proposal: For unequal extremal side indices, choose B in T by strict lexicographic comparison of the whole equal-length suffix from j+1 through |x|, instead of truncating at the later extremal side index. A=T minus B.
mathematical_findings: B0 from manuscript remains subset of B by its strict first difference at the later extremal side index; same cylinder lower tail applies.
A and B depend only on columns other than j, so actual partial-reveal sampling law applies once atom invariance proved.
A union B=T subset R preserves sample-complement lower bound g even when B enlarges.
Residual marked and unmarked counts have conditional means(n-|A|)p and(n-|A|)q, still at least g*n*p and g*n*q.
Prefix-x rows have equal compared suffix and lie in A. On B, before-x classification is digit<=x_j in less-suffix case and digit<x_j in greater-suffix case.
Original failure and variance constants unchanged; no public hypothesis or frozen contract change.
adversarial_findings: Suffix comparison must end at |x|, not at global future length d; otherwise a prefix-x row with further digits could be falsely classified.
Works when x=v since later extremal index<=|v|; no strict descendant premise.
Rows whose first suffix difference is later than source witness cutoff enlarge B harmlessly; B0 inclusion and sample complement suffice.
limitations: This review approves mathematics/interface, not yet a checked Lean construction.
Need explicit equal-length suffix lemmas, atom invariance, shift measurability, B0 inclusion, good-event bound and variance proof.
